daniil_b.name: Daniil Porfiryevich Bondarenko
daniil_b.bio: Son of Porfiry Bondarenko and a career officer. He fought in the Soviet-Finnish War and the Second World War and finished his service as a colonel.
facts: Drafted on 9 Dec 1939; took part in the Soviet-Finnish War of 1939–1940.
81st Rifle Regiment, 54th Rifle Division; Kem Operational Group, Karelian Front.
Major, senior assistant to the head of the section for applying war experience, operations department, 26th Army staff.
Lieutenant → Senior Lieutenant → Captain → Major → Colonel.
Order of the Patriotic War, 2nd and 1st class; Medal “For Victory over Germany”.

facts.t: He served in Kyiv, knew Fidel Castro and gave him two parrots.

porfiry.name: Porfiry Vlasovich Bondarenko
porfiry.bio: Grenadier of the 12th Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment of Emperor Alexander III; Orthodox, married, from the village of Zaliman, Izyum district, Kharkov Governorate. Wounded in September 1916 near Zaturtsy in Volhynia, in November he received the St George Cross, 4th class, No. 734616.
facts: Wounded on 21 Sep 1916 near Zaturtsy; evacuated through the dressing unit of the Moscow exchange and merchant societies.
St George Cross, 4th class, No. 734616, awarded at a review on 16 Nov 1916.

facts.t: The cross was presented by Grand Duke George Mikhailovich:
facts.tr: in the name of His Majesty the Emperor

facts: The award is also recorded by S. B. Patrikeev in the consolidated lists of St George Cross holders, 1914–1922, vol. 11.

facts.t: Family tradition: “a gold cross, given by the Tsar himself”; he was lame or had lost a leg. The 4th-class cross was silver, but it was indeed presented by a member of the imperial family in the Tsar's name, so the tradition is nearly accurate.

porfiry.title: Porfiry Bondarenko
porfiry.subtitle: St George cavalier from the village of Zaliman

sections.heading: A reserve soldier's son
sections.text: The Zaliman parish register calls his father, Vlas Savelyevich, a private. Service was already part of this family's life: Porfiry's uncle Evgraf is recorded as a private too.

quote.tr: private, of the village of Zaliman

sections.heading: Grenadier of the Astrakhan Regiment
sections.text: Porfiry serves in the 12th Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment of Emperor Alexander III. The records describe him briefly: Orthodox, married, Kharkov Governorate, Izyum district, Savintsy volost, village of Zaliman.

sections.heading: Wounded near Zaturtsy
sections.text: In Volhynia, near the village of Zaturtsy, the grenadier is wounded. He is evacuated through the dressing unit of the Moscow exchange and merchant societies, as a casualty bureau card records.

sections.heading: Cross No. 734616
sections.text: Singled out for particular distinction, Porfiry receives the St George Cross, 4th class, at a review. It is presented by Grand Duke George Mikhailovich. The award survives in the regimental list and in S. B. Patrikeev's consolidated lists of recipients.

quote.tr: in the name of His Majesty the Emperor

sections.heading: “A gold cross, given by the Tsar himself”
sections.text: The family said that the cross was gold and came from the Tsar himself, and that Porfiry was left lame or without a leg. A 4th-class cross was silver, but it was indeed presented by a member of the imperial family in the Tsar's name. Family memory proved nearly exact.

sections.heading: Home in Zaliman
sections.text: With Maria Simeonovna he raises children in his native village. Anastasia is born in 1918 and the twins Andrey and Afanasy in 1919; Andrey dies at two days old. Daniil, the future colonel, is born in 1921.

daniil.title: Daniil Bondarenko
daniil.subtitle: Colonel, son of a St George cavalier

sections.heading: The first war
sections.text: On 9 December 1939, shortly before turning eighteen, the son of the St George cavalier is drafted and takes part in the Soviet-Finnish War.

sections.heading: The Karelian Front
sections.text: 81st Rifle Regiment of the 54th Rifle Division, then the Kem Operational Group of the Karelian Front. By 1944 he is a major and senior assistant to the head of the section for applying war experience in the operations department of the 26th Army staff.

sections.heading: The award sheet
sections.text: Order of the Patriotic War, 2nd class. With a radio station among units of the 205th Rifle Division he secured the army commander's control of the troops during the pursuit on the Kestenga axis; he also served as duty operations officer and compiled combat experience.

sections.heading: Two orders and a medal
sections.text: Order of the Patriotic War, 2nd class; Order of the Patriotic War, 1st class; and the Medal “For Victory over Germany”.

sections.heading: Two parrots for Fidel
sections.text: The family says that Daniil served in Kyiv, knew Fidel Castro and gave him two parrots. Castro did visit Kyiv in May 1963 and January 1964; the meeting itself has not yet been documented.

sections.heading: The line of service continues
sections.text: According to the family, his son Evgeny became head of civil defence for Kharkiv and its region. A grenadier of 1916, a colonel, a head of civil defence: three generations of service.

zaliman.title: Zaliman
zaliman.subtitle: The family's home on the Siverskyi Donets
paragraphs: Zaliman was founded around 1671 on the bank of the Siverskyi Donets, opposite Savintsy. Its people were state peasants of the Izyum district in Kharkov Governorate.
The village later belonged to the Balakliia and then the Izium district of Kharkiv region. The Narozhnyis, Berezhnoys and Bondarenkos appear here side by side in the same parish registers.
zaliman.estate_text: Documents of 1903 describe the people of Zaliman as state peasants; those of 1918–1919 as peasants of the settlement of Zaliman. No noble roots have been found.

estate_quote.tr: peasants of the settlement of Zaliman

facts_page.title: Curious facts
facts_page.subtitle: Small discoveries from the archives and family lore
facts_page.note: Illustrations come from Wikimedia Commons; the author and licence are given under each image. Document scans come from the family archive and the archives named in the captions.

izum_polk.title: The Izyum Sloboda Regiment and the Donets-Zakharzhevskys
izum_polk.text: Until 1765 Zaliman belonged to the Izyum Sloboda Cossack Regiment. The regiment was formed in 1685 to defend against Crimean Tatar raids, and by 1732 it had 17 companies (sotnias). In its first decades it was led by colonels of the Donets-Zakharzhevsky family, one of the most distinguished in Sloboda Ukraine, so the Zaliman ancestors of that time most likely served under them, although no document names specific ancestors. The family has died out; Donets-Zakharzhevska Street in Kharkiv still recalls it.
izum_polk.source: N. Gerbel, 'The Izyum Sloboda Cossack Regiment, 1651–1765' (St Petersburg, 1852); no document on specific ancestors
izum_polk.image: Coat of arms of the Donets-Zakharzhevsky family

free_village.title: A free village without a landlord
free_village.text: In the 1782 census of the 'Cherkasy' (Cossack settlers) of the Izyum district, Zaliman has no landowner. The 1903 parish register explicitly calls its people 'state peasants'. So the ancestors were never serfs.
free_village.source: DAKhO, f. 31, op. 141, spr. 18 (1782 census); DAKhO, f. 40, op. 139, spr. 228 (1903 parish register)
free_village.image: Map of the Izyum district from the 'Topographic Description of the Kharkov Viceroyalty', 1788

flu_1918.title: The Spanish flu of 1918
flu_1918.text: According to the annual summary of the parish register, 144 children were born in Zaliman in 1918, 73 weddings took place and 97 people died, many of them in the epidemic. It was in this year, on 13 April, that great-grandmother Anastasia Porfiryevna was born.

georgy_crosses.title: More than a million 'Georges'
georgy_crosses.text: The soldiers' St George Cross was the highest award for the lower ranks. By November 1916 about 1.37 million men had received it. Among them was the grenadier Porfiry Bondarenko: Cross, 4th class, No. 734616.
georgy_crosses.source: Award list of the 12th Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment (RGVIA, f. 970); S. B. Patrikeev's consolidated lists of recipients
georgy_crosses.image: Insignia of the Military Order (St George Cross), 4th class, silver. National Museum of the Republic of Tatarstan

astrakhan.title: The Emperor's regiment
astrakhan.text: Porfiry served in the 12th Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment, one of the oldest in the Russian army: it was formed in 1700 under Peter I. Its colonel-in-chief was Emperor Alexander III, so the regiment bore his name.
astrakhan.source: Sytin's 'Military Encyclopedia', vol. 3 (St Petersburg, 1911), article on the 12th Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment
astrakhan.image: Colonel's standard of the Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment, 1797 (reconstruction)

romanov_cross.title: A cross from a Romanov's hands
romanov_cross.text: On 16 November 1916 the cross was presented to Porfiry by Grand Duke George Mikhailovich, a grandson of Emperor Nicholas I, who was touring the front on behalf of the reigning Emperor Nicholas II. They were two different people: the Grand Duke was a cousin of Nicholas II's father, Alexander III. Hence the family story that 'the Tsar himself gave the award'. George Mikhailovich was a noted coin collector; in 1919 he was shot by the Bolsheviks.
romanov_cross.source: Award list of the 12th Astrakhan Grenadier Regiment (RGVIA, f. 970): 'in the name of His Majesty the Emperor'

brusilov.title: The Brusilov Offensive
brusilov.text: Porfiry was wounded on 21 September 1916 near the village of Zaturtsy in Volhynia, during the later stage of the Brusilov Offensive, one of the largest offensives of the First World War.
brusilov.source: Card of the casualty registration bureau ('In Memory of the Heroes of the Great War')
brusilov.image: Offensive of the South-Western Front, summer 1916. Map from the Granat Encyclopedic Dictionary

daniil_staff.title: An army staff major in 1944
daniil_staff.text: Daniil Porfiryevich (born 1921) went to the Soviet-Finnish War in 1939, shortly before turning eighteen, and by 1944 he was a major in the operations department of the 26th Army staff on the Karelian Front. His award sheet says that, with a radio station among units of the 205th Rifle Division, he kept the army commander in contact with the troops.
daniil_staff.source: Award sheet of 9 Oct 1944, 'Memory of the People' database

castro.title: Parrots for Fidel
castro.text: Family lore says that Daniil served in Kyiv and gave Fidel Castro two parrots. Castro really did visit Kyiv twice, in May 1963 and in January 1964.
castro.source: Family lore; visit dates from publications on Fidel Castro's trips to the USSR
castro.image: Kyiv, 1961: view from Bohdan Khmelnytsky Street towards Khreshchatyk

twins.title: Twin brothers
twins.text: On 30 November 1919 Porfiry and Maria had twins, Andrey and Afanasy. Andrey lived only two days. Afanasy's fate is still unknown.

today.title: Zaliman today
today.text: The village stands on the Siverskyi Donets, opposite Savintsy. In 2022 it was under occupation for about a month and was badly damaged.
